questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: y = 100(1.08)^t is rewritten as y = 100 · 2^(t/9.01). Why does the rewritten form show the doubling time?
questions.prompt_markup: y = 100(1.08)^t is rewritten as y = 100 · 2^(t/9.01). Why does the rewritten form show the doubling time?

choices.text: Because 9.01 is the growth rate in percent per year, and doubling depends only on the rate.
Because 2 is the starting value, and the exponent t/9.01 counts how many times it is used.
Because y = 200 when t = 1, so y doubles from 100 to 200 in the first year and in each 9.01-year period.
The exponent t/9.01 increases by 1 every 9.01 years, and each such increase multiplies y by 2.

questions.correct_answer: The exponent t/9.01 increases by 1 every 9.01 years, and each such increase multiplies y by 2.
questions.grading_note: Base 2 with exponent t/T doubles every T units. The others misread the parts (100 is the starting value; the rate is 8%).
